title: GitHub Actions Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the GitHub Actions lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: A workflow file
entries.summary: A workflow describes jobs GitHub Actions can run for a repository. The YAML file lives under .github/workflows.

example.code:
name: Say hello
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Hello, club"

notes: Running hosted workflows uses the service's permissions and usage rules; no run is needed to read this course.

entries.name: Events start workflows
entries.summary: An event tells GitHub when to consider running a workflow. workflow_dispatch is manual; push reacts to selected pushed changes.
notes: A filter must match the real branch name to react to its pushes.

entries.name: Jobs and steps
entries.summary: A job runs a list of steps on a runner. Steps in one job run in order and share that job's working environment.

example.code:
jobs:
  explain:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: First step
        run: echo "Read"
      - name: Second step
        run: echo "Check"

notes: Do not assume a file from one job appears in another job automatically.

entries.name: Runners execute jobs
entries.summary: A runner is the machine environment that executes a job. runs-on chooses a matching runner label.
notes: latest is a moving label, not a permanent operating-system version.

entries.name: Name steps clearly
entries.summary: Step names appear in the run log. Clear names help someone find the part that failed.

example.code:
steps:
  - name: Show working directory
    run: pwd
  - name: Print learning message
    run: echo "Read the result"

notes: A step name should describe its action, not claim it passed.

entries.name: Environment values
entries.summary: env gives a job or step named environment values. A shell can read them without repeating the literal text in each command.

example.code:
env:
  CLUB_NAME: Reading club
steps:
  - run: echo "$CLUB_NAME"

notes: Ordinary environment values in source are not a safe place for credentials.

entries.name: Job dependencies
entries.summary: needs makes a job wait for another job to succeed. This states the order between jobs.

example.code:
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Check"
  report:
    needs: check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Checks finished"

notes: A dependency does not copy files between jobs.

entries.name: Matrices repeat a job
entries.summary: A matrix runs variations of a job. Each combination gets its own job run.

example.code:
strategy:
  matrix:
    fruit: [apple, pear]
steps:
  - run: echo "${{ matrix.fruit }}"

notes: A large matrix multiplies work and usage; choose useful cases.

entries.name: Limit token permissions
entries.summary: The workflow token can be given small permissions. Give only the access a job actually needs.
notes: Do not give broad write permissions to untrusted changes.

entries.name: Handle untrusted text as data
entries.summary: A workflow may receive text from a pull request. Do not paste untrusted text directly into a shell script; pass it as data and quote it.

example.code:
env:
  NOTE: A fixed practice message
steps:
  - run: printf "%s\n" "$NOTE"

notes: Never execute a message or title as if it were a trusted command.

entries.name: Avoid duplicate obsolete runs
entries.summary: Concurrency can group related runs. cancel-in-progress can stop an older run when a newer run in the same group starts.
notes: Do not blindly cancel a deployment or other action that has important partial effects.

entries.name: Read the run result
entries.summary: A run log shows which jobs and steps completed. A green result means the configured commands passed, not that every product requirement was checked.

example.code:
Check run:
  syntax check: passed
  unit tests: passed
  visual review: not part of this workflow

notes: Never print real secrets just to diagnose a workflow.
